newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek '97 fx policy won't set volatility aim - paper.
newsitem.headline: Greek '97 fx policy won't set volatility aim - paper.

text.p: The Greek government and the central bank have decided against setting a volatility target for the drachma in 1997, said the daily Imerisia on Wednesday.
The report was cited earleir by a trader as a reason for a firmer ecu/drachma. Ecu/drachma was trading around 304.20/30 at 1330 local (1130 GMT).

The Bank of Greece has adopted in the last few years a so-called 'hard drachma' policy, which aims to combat inflation by letting the drachma slide against some major European currencies, mainly the ecu, by less than that justified by inflation differentials between Greece and its major trading partners.
The ecu/drachma cross has been used as a yardstick, and the central bank managed to contain the drachma's depreciation against the ecu at 1.0 percent in 1996 and 3.0 percent in 1996.
The central bank is not expected to set an explicit ecu/drachma target for 1997 to avoid inviting speculative forex inflows and boosting liquidity that might endanger its crusade against inflation.
Central bank officials have said that they favoured a more volatile ecu/drachma in 1997 to discourage speculative inflows.

The central bank is also expected to cut gradually its intervention rates in line with developments on the fiscal front, inflation, money supply, the drachma and interest rate trends on some major european currencies.
It is also expected to use repo operations to smooth out interbank liquidity.
Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos is expected to announce 1997 monetary policy in late January. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
